literal: The Eleven Princes of Gaozu
idiomatic: The Eleven Princes of Shenwu

literal: Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You; Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu; Prince of Rencheng Hui; Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Prince of Huashan Ning; Prince of Fengyi Run; Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia
idiomatic: Prince Jianping of Yong'an (Jun); Prince Jingyi of Pingyang (Yan); Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng (You); Prince Gangsu of Shangdang (Huan); Prince Jing of Xiangcheng (Yu); Prince of Rencheng (Hui); Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang (Shi); Prince Wenjian of Boling (Ji); Prince of Huashan (Ning); Prince of Fengyi (Run); Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang (Qia)

literal: The Shenwu Emperor had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Emperor Wenxiang, Emperor Wenxuan, Emperor Xiaozhao, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Emperor Wucheng, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Hui; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, the Shenwu Emperor, had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Gao Cheng, Gao Yang, Gao Yan, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Gao Zhan, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Hui; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.

literal: Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, style name Dingle, was the third son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Jianping of Yong'an (Jun), whose style name was Dingle, was the third son of Gao Huan.

literal: At first, when Shenwu took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born, he suspected the child was not of his kind and did not love him greatly.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan first took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born he doubted the child was truly his and showed little affection.

literal: Yet Jun was precocious, and afterward came to be favored.
idiomatic: Yet Jun was precocious, and in time he came to be favored.

literal: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.'
idiomatic: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.'

literal: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"
idiomatic: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"

literal: He replied:
idiomatic: He replied:

literal: "There is."
idiomatic: "There is."

literal: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"
idiomatic: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"

literal: Jingyu could not answer.
idiomatic: Jingyu could not answer.

literal: When he grew up, he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was heavily beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.
idiomatic: When he grew up he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was severely beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.

literal: Later he somewhat reformed his ways and took reading as his occupation.
idiomatic: Later he somewhat reformed his conduct and devoted himself to study.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.

literal: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Wenxiang.
idiomatic: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Gao Cheng.

literal: Wenxuan's nature was timid and weak; whenever he attended upon Wenxiang, tears sometimes fell.
idiomatic: Gao Yang was by nature timid and effeminate; whenever he attended upon Gao Cheng, tears would sometimes fall.

literal: Jun often rebuked those at the Emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe the elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.
idiomatic: Jun often rebuked those at the emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe his elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

literal: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting; intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.
idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting, yet intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to princely rank.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was advanced to princely rank.

literal: In the last years of Wenxuan's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.
idiomatic: In the last years of Gao Yang's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.

literal: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will use me."
idiomatic: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will heed me."

literal: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the Emperor, and again he came to be resented.
idiomatic: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the emperor, and again he came to be resented.

literal: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the Emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.

literal: The Emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.
idiomatic: The emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.

literal: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.
idiomatic: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.

literal: The Emperor was greatly displeased.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly displeased.

literal: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.
idiomatic: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.

literal: The Emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.
idiomatic: The emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.

literal: The Emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"

literal: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.
idiomatic: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.

literal: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.
idiomatic: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.

literal: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.
idiomatic: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.

literal: The Emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.
idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.

literal: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.
idiomatic: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.

literal: The next year the Emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.
idiomatic: The next year the emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.

literal: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.
idiomatic: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.

literal: The Emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.
idiomatic: The emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.

literal: Prince Changguang Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "Can a fierce beast safely be let out of its den?"
idiomatic: Prince Changguang Gao Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "Can a fierce beast safely be let out of its den?"

literal: The Emperor fell silent.
idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

literal: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"
idiomatic: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"

literal: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.
idiomatic: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.

literal: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the Emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.
idiomatic: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.

literal: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.
idiomatic: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.

literal: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.
idiomatic: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.

literal: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.
idiomatic: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.

literal: Later the Emperor gave Jun's consort Lady Lu in marriage to Palace Attendant Equal to the Third Rank Liu Yujie — a former personal attendant of the Emperor who had been employed for military merit; at the time he had ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and therefore she was given to him.
idiomatic: Later the emperor gave Jun's consort Lady Lu in marriage to Palace Attendant Equal to the Third Rank Liu Yujie — a former personal attendant of the emperor who had been employed for military merit; at the time he had ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and therefore she was given to him.

literal: Several days later the Emperor, because Lady Lu had never been favored by Jun, ordered that the marriage be severed.
idiomatic: Several days later the emperor, because Lady Lu had never been favored by Jun, ordered that the marriage be severed.

literal: In the first year of Qianming he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant.

literal: Having no sons, an edict appointed Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You's second son Zhun as heir.
idiomatic: Having no sons, an edict appointed Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You's second son Zhun as heir.

literal: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng, You, style name Zishen, was the fifth son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng (You), whose style name was Zishen, was the fifth son of Gao Huan.

literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.
idiomatic: In the second year of the Yuanxiang era he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.

literal: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."
idiomatic: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."

literal: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.
idiomatic: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.

literal: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like — why must one always boast of one's handwriting?
idiomatic: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like — why must one always boast of one's handwriting?

literal: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"
idiomatic: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"

literal: He was then about eight years old.
idiomatic: He was then about eight years old.

literal: Yi was deeply ashamed.
idiomatic: Yi was deeply ashamed.

literal: In the sixth year of Wuding he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Wuding era he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.

literal: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.
idiomatic: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.

literal: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.
idiomatic: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.

literal: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.
idiomatic: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.

literal: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"
idiomatic: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"

literal: Da immediately confessed his guilt.
idiomatic: Da immediately confessed his guilt.

literal: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.
idiomatic: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.

literal: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.
idiomatic: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.

literal: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.
idiomatic: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.

literal: The next morning he reported it to the province.
idiomatic: The next morning he reported it to the province.

literal: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.
idiomatic: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.

literal: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.
idiomatic: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.

literal: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.

literal: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.
idiomatic: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.

literal: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."
idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."

literal: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.
idiomatic: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.

literal: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.

literal: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.
idiomatic: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.

literal: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.
idiomatic: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.

literal: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.
idiomatic: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.

literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.

literal: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.
idiomatic: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.

literal: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."
idiomatic: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."

literal: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.
idiomatic: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.

literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.

literal: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.
idiomatic: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.

literal: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.
idiomatic: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.

literal: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."
idiomatic: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."

literal: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.
idiomatic: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.

literal: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.
idiomatic: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.

literal: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.
idiomatic: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.

literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.

literal: When Wucheng succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhan succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

literal: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.
idiomatic: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.

literal: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.
idiomatic: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.

literal: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.
idiomatic: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.

literal: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.
idiomatic: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.

literal: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.
idiomatic: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.
